_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), set 31/5/1. 32 pages (idx 0-31): idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-30, Hindi on every odd index 3-29 (each the Hindi of the page after it); idx 31 is blank apart from the barcode and '550-1' footer. Odd-page tops checked on the contact sheet and idx 15 + idx 25 at full size: all Hindi, no English overflow. The alternation held throughout, no parity inversion; last English page idx 30 (Q39 (a)-(c)). Question numbers run 1-39 unbroken. Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the 31/5/1 marking scheme (ms p02-p09) for a bare OR: OR in Q23, 25, 28, 34, 35, 36, 37(c), 38(c), 39(c) = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. Q25's OR is INSIDE part (B) only (see its _flag). The paper labels whole-question alternatives (A)/(B) and their parts (a)/(b); questionNumber follows the corpus convention '23 (a)' / '37 (c) (i)'. All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme image (ms p02); each was re-derived and agrees; no void note anywhere in the scheme. Decimal points on this PAPER are ordinary full stops (1.44, 0.01, 0.25); the scheme prints raised dots. Opener of series 31/5: nothing skipped (plan.txt: no reference papers).

questions.context: In human beings, there are 23 pairs of chromosomes. Out of these 23 pairs of chromosomes (i.e. 46 chromosomes), 22 pairs of chromosomes are called autosomes and one pair of chromosomes. i.e. two chromosomes are called sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types – ‘X’ chromosomes and ‘Y’ chromosomes. The sex of a child (i.e. progeny), is decided at the time of fertilisation. In other words, at the time of zygote formation the sex chromosomes inherited from the parents of a child decide whether the new born will be a boy or a girl.
